task: vector_addition extension complete canonical frontend matrix audit
conclusions: Original wrapper only asserts CUDA device membership; it has no dtype, matching shape/length, contiguous-stride, or same-device assertion. output is empty_like(x), and n_elements is output.numel().

The 17 representative Torch dtypes map to 17 distinct canonical Triton scalar signatures: bool, signed/unsigned 8/16/32/64, fp16/bf16/fp32/fp64, and four fp8 formats. Runtime table additionally maps shell torch.int1/torch.uint1 to the same u1 signature as bool; their allocator/storage domain is uncharacterized. Recognition and frontend generation do not establish CUDA allocator or native backend support.

Mixed tensor promotion: fp64 dominates; then fp32; then fp16. bf16+bf16 stays bf16, remaining bf16 mixtures use fp32. Identical fp8 stays that format; different fp8 uses fp16. fp8+integer/bool directly raises TypeError.

Integer promotion does not widen small equal-width operands to int32: same signedness uses wider width; mixed signedness selects unsigned at equal/greater unsigned width, otherwise signed wider width. The final addition is arith.addi at that width and requires modular bitvector semantics in ordinary non-debug execution. Raw frontend IR also includes overflow-sanitizer calculations/assertions; this probe does not lower them or prove the debug/error domain.

tl.store casts to x pointer element dtype. Bool pointer is first reinterpreted as int8, then value cast to int8; mixed bool output is not modeled by a general nonzero-to-bool store. Bool+bool uses i1 addition before zero-extending to stored i8.
Float downcast defaults RTNE. Float/integer casts use signed/unsigned conversion and need explicit out-of-range/NaN semantics. Integer truncation and signed extension are visible in frontend IR.
Current vector_addition Kernels.lean uses RegionName (real), no source dtype parameter or promotion/store dispatch. Existing per-program fp32 theorem cannot cover all native branches.

DSL has typed fp16/bf16/fp32/f8e4/f8e5 channels and an explicit ComputeDType.fp64 annotation/raw Float64Bits representation, so float64 is not wholly absent. There is no distinct fp64 TileDType, and current kernel does not bind fp64 provenance; native binary64 arithmetic/cast correspondence remains to establish.

DSL int/nat channels use unbounded Int/Nat addition, not per-dtype modular arithmetic. FixedInteger and unsigned/signed cast helpers can express explicit conversions, but current kernel has no width-preserving automatic integer arithmetic or full signed/unsigned promotion matrix.

The fp8e4b8 (Torch float8_e4m3fnuz) same-type frontend probe is rejected at sm90 with unsupported-architecture dtype; this is a checked frontend failure, not a claim about all architectures. Only two fp8 storage channels exist in TileDType. Distinct fnuz fp8 formats need separate semantics or explicit unsupported-runtime characterization; canonical Torch fp8 names alone do not prove native support.
Unknown canonical Torch shell/complex/quantized dtypes remain explicitly uncharacterized here; absence from the runtime canonicalization table is recorded, not claimed as a full host error proof.

Masked tl.load has no other argument, so inactive lanes contain unspecified values. Arithmetic may evaluate those lanes, but stores are masked; any finite-input premise over every lane must account for this source behavior.
remaining_work: Compile the complete source-bound 17x17 native backend matrix at each intended architecture, separating frontend promotion errors and lowering failures (especially fp8/fp64 and fnuz).
Prove dtype dispatch/promotion/storage casts and integer wrapping, or characterize exact error branches. These are structural scope gaps, not deferrable numerical assumptions.
Bind native Torch allocation/layout/device/error behavior; prove valid physical address bounds for both inputs and output despite missing shape/stride checks.
For newly represented FP arithmetic/casts, register narrowly scoped numerical assumptions and preserve exceptional-value domain.
